subject: Physics
title: Oscillations
summary: A motion that repeats after equal intervals is periodic; back-and-forth periodic motion about a mean position is oscillation.
Simple harmonic motion (SHM) happens when the restoring force is proportional to displacement and opposite to it: F = −kx. Then x = A sin(ωt + φ) with ω = √(k/m).
In SHM, speed is maximum at the mean position and zero at the extremes; acceleration is the opposite. Total energy ½kA² stays constant, shared between KE and PE.
Spring–mass: T = 2π√(m/k). Simple pendulum (small angle): T = 2π√(l/g), independent of mass and amplitude.

formulas.name: Periodic motion
formulas.when: Converting time period, frequency and angular frequency.

formulas.name: SHM condition
formulas.when: Testing whether a motion is SHM.
formulas.mistake: A uniform circular motion projected on a diameter is SHM, but a bouncing ball is periodic, not SHM.

formulas.name: Displacement in SHM
formulas.formula: x = A sin(ωt + φ)  (or A cos(ωt + φ))
formulas.when: Position at any time; φ is the initial phase.

formulas.name: Velocity in SHM
formulas.formula: v = Aω cos(ωt + φ) = ±ω√(A² − x²);   v_max = Aω (at x = 0)

formulas.name: Acceleration in SHM
formulas.formula: a = −ω² x;   a_max = ω² A (at x = ±A)
formulas.when: Force and acceleration at the extremes.
formulas.note: Acceleration is always towards the mean position — opposite to x.

formulas.name: Energy in SHM
formulas.formula: KE = ½ k(A² − x²);  PE = ½ k x²;  E = ½ k A² = ½ m ω² A²
formulas.mistake: KE = PE at x = A/√2, not at A/2.

formulas.name: Spring–mass system
formulas.when: Mass on a spring (horizontal or vertical).
formulas.note: For a vertical spring the same formula holds — gravity only shifts the mean position.

formulas.name: Cut spring
formulas.formula: k ∝ 1/length: cutting a spring into n equal parts gives each part nk

formulas.name: Simple pendulum
formulas.mistake: T does not depend on the mass of the bob or the amplitude (for small swings).

formulas.name: Pendulum with effective g
formulas.formula: T = 2π√(l/g_eff);  lift accelerating up: g + a;  down: g − a;  car with horizontal a: √(g² + a²)
formulas.when: Pendulums in lifts and accelerating vehicles.

formulas.name: Phase relations
formulas.formula: velocity leads displacement by π/2;  acceleration leads displacement by π

examples.title: Reading an SHM equation
examples.problem: x = 5 sin(πt + π/3) cm. Find amplitude, period, maximum speed and maximum acceleration.
examples.solution: A = 5 cm, ω = π rad/s → T = 2π/ω = 2 s. v_max = Aω ≈ 15.7 cm/s, a_max = Aω² ≈ 49.3 cm/s².

examples.solution: ½k(A² − x²) = ½kx² → x = A/√2 ≈ 7.07 cm.

topics.title: Periodic functions
topics.explain: sin ωt and cos ωt repeat every 2π/ω, so any periodic motion can be described with them. Functions like sin ωt + cos ωt are still SHM (amplitude √2, phase shifted); sin² ωt is periodic with period π/ω.

topics.title: SHM and circular motion
topics.explain: The projection of a particle moving uniformly on a circle onto any diameter performs SHM. The radius is the amplitude and the angular speed is ω — handy for finding time between two positions.

topics.title: Graphs of SHM
topics.explain: x, v and a are all sinusoidal with the same ω. v is π/2 ahead of x, a is π ahead of x. The v–x graph is an ellipse; the a–x graph is a straight line with negative slope.

topics.title: Energy graphs
topics.explain: Potential energy (PE) is a parabola with minimum at x = 0; kinetic energy (KE) is an inverted parabola; their sum is a horizontal line. KE and PE each oscillate with frequency 2ν (double the SHM frequency).

topics.title: Restoring force and force constant
topics.explain: The spring constant k tells how stiff the system is. For any SHM, ω² = (restoring force per unit displacement)/(mass). For the pendulum, the restoring force mg sinθ ≈ mgθ gives ω² = g/l.

topics.title: Deriving the pendulum period
topics.explain: Torque about the pivot −mgl sinθ ≈ −mglθ; with I = ml², α = −(g/l)θ. Comparing with α = −ω²θ gives T = 2π√(l/g).

topics.title: Time between positions
topics.explain: From the mean to an extreme takes T/4. From the mean to A/2 takes T/12; from A/2 to A takes T/6. From the mean to A/√2 takes T/8.
